He later served as co-chairman before retiring from executive leadership.

long_biography.plain_text:
The Berwind enterprise came to Charles Graham Berwind Jr. through a family trust holding company shares. He joined the business after studying at Vermont and Harvard and serving in the Coast Guard, then took the chair when his father died. The transferred stake carried an operating mandate: he consolidated family control, acquired the pharmaceutical-coatings company Colorcon and widened the group beyond its mining base.

For a quarter-century, Berwind combined chairmanship, presidency and chief executive authority. By the time he stepped back, the old coal concern had become an investment group with manufacturing, service, property and financial businesses. He remained co-chairman until 2006, leaving a family enterprise whose structure reflected both transferred ownership and his own long operating tenure.
